# IEEE GRSS Data Fusion Contest 2026 - Complete Information

## CONTEST OVERVIEW

**Title:** IEEE GRSS Data Fusion Contest 2026 - SAR Temporal Storytelling

**Organizing Bodies:**
- Image Analysis and Data Fusion Technical Committee (IADF TC) of GRSS
- Capella Space

**Contest Focus:** Commercial high-resolution Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery analysis with emphasis on temporal stacking, change detection, and time-series analysis

---

## CONTEST STRUCTURE & PHASES

**Single Phase Format:**
- Participants receive all relevant data at contest opening
- Develop, explore, and evaluate methods throughout contest period
- May use any analytical or visualization approach

**Submission Requirements:**
- Concise document (initial phase)
- 4-page IEEE-style paper (final phase for winners)
- IGARSS 2026 fullpaper template required
- Must include names and affiliations of all team members
- No team member additions after initial submission

---

## TIMELINE & DEADLINES

| Date | Event |
|------|-------|
| **February 4, 2026** | Contest opening and data release; evaluation committee begins accepting submissions |
| **April 6, 2026** | Submission deadline (evaluation committee stops accepting entries) |
| **April 13, 2026** | Winner announcement |
| **April 20, 2026** | Internal deadline for papers; DFC Committee review process |
| **April 28, 2026** | Final paper submission deadline for IGARSS publication |
| **August 9-14, 2026** | Presentation at DFC-dedicated IGARSS 2026 Session (Washington, USA) |

---

## DATASET SPECIFICATIONS

### Dataset Overview
- **Multiple densely sampled temporal stacks** of very high-resolution SAR imagery
- **Collected by:** Capella Space satellite constellation (X-band SAR)
- **Approximately 1,582 unique collects** organized in coordinated stacks
- **17,000+ possible image pairs** available
- **Emphasis:** Real-world operational diversity, not synthetic benchmarks

### Geographic Coverage
- Global distribution across diverse regions
- Deep temporal stacks over some areas (multiple acquisitions across the year)
- Spans wide range of imaging geometries, acquisition modes, and operational conditions
- Multiple scene types (urban, infrastructure, agriculture, etc.)

### Data Products Available

1. **Single Look Complex (SLC)** - Complex-valued SAR imagery with phase information; enables interferometric processing and time-series deformation studies

2. **Geocoded (GEO)** - Image-domain representations projected to geographic coordinate system; facilitates visualization and integration with other geospatial data

3. **Complex Phase History Data (CPHD)** - Select collects provided; raw phase history measurements prior to image formation; enables custom processing and experimental approaches

4. **Geocoded Ellipsoid Corrected (GEC)** - Geocoded imagery with ellipsoid correction to help exclude terrain artifacts

### Imaging Modes

1. **Spotlight Mode**
   - Highest spatial resolution
   - Continuously illuminates fixed ground location
   - Enables detailed characterization of fine-scale structures

2. **Sliding Spotlight (Spotlight Wide)**
   - Extended scene coverage
   - Gradual antenna pointing during collection
   - Balance between high spatial resolution and coverage

3. **Stripmap Mode**
   - Fixed antenna pointing
   - Wider-area coverage
   - Consistent geometry
   - Moderate resolution
   - Suitable for large-scale monitoring

### CSV Metadata Fields

The accompanying CSV file contains the following metadata for each collect pair:

- **collect_id_ref:** Unique identifier for primary (reference) SAR acquisition
- **collect_id_sec:** Unique identifier for matched secondary SAR acquisition
- **start_time_ref:** Acquisition start time of reference collect (UTC)
- **start_time_sec:** Acquisition start time of secondary collect (UTC)
- **platform_ref:** Satellite platform that acquired reference collect
- **platform_sec:** Satellite platform that acquired secondary collect
- **polarization_ref:** Transmit-receive polarization of reference collect
- **polarization_sec:** Transmit-receive polarization of secondary collect
- **mode:** SAR imaging mode (Spotlight, Sliding Spotlight, Stripmap)
- **look_direction:** Side-looking geometry (left or right looking)
- **flight_direction:** Orbit direction (ascending or descending)
- **incidence_ref:** Incidence angle of reference collect at scene center (degrees)
- **incidence_sec:** Incidence angle of secondary collect at scene center (degrees)
- **dif_incidence:** Absolute difference in incidence angle between reference and secondary (degrees)
- **delta_graze_deg:** Difference in grazing angle between reference and secondary (degrees)
- **latitude:** Latitude of scene center (degrees)
- **longitude:** Longitude of scene center (degrees)
- **height:** Height above reference ellipsoid or MSL at scene center

---

## ANALYSIS POSSIBILITIES

Participants can pursue a diverse range of analytical approaches:

1. **Interferometric Analysis**
   - Temporal stacking for interferometric change analysis
   - Time-series deformation studies using SLC products

2. **Spotlight Processing**
   - Long-dwell, high-resolution spotlight-style collections
   - Aperture diversity exploitation
   - Geometric prior-based approaches

3. **Pattern-of-Life & Activity Characterization**
   - Temporal stacks for persistent change detection
   - Episodic event identification
   - Evolving scene dynamics over time

4. **Application Domains** (Encouraged)
   - Land cover classification
   - Infrastructure monitoring
   - Environmental change detection
   - Urban development tracking
   - Agricultural monitoring
   - Any other creative applications

**Core Motivation:** Encourage development of robust algorithms, particularly for participants using deep neural networks (DNNs), that leverage temporal information and diverse acquisition geometries

---

## DATA ACCESS & RESOURCES

### Data Access Methods

1. **AWS S3 Bucket (Public)**
   - Openly downloadable from Capella Space Open Data repository
   - Can access without authentication
   - Select specific datasets or assets directly from S3

2. **STAC Catalog**
   - Published STAC (SpatioTemporal Asset Catalog) collection
   - URL: https://stacindex.org/catalogs/capella-space-opendata
   - Enables query and filtering capabilities

3. **Interactive Felt Map**
   - Browse data interactively through provided felt map
   - Visualize geographic distribution of collects

### Tutorials & Learning Resources

- **Access and Download:** STAC Catalog documentation
- **Python Notebook:** Examples on querying and filtering STAC collections
- **QGIS Guide:** Scaling GEO Images in QGIS (by Capella Space)
- **GEO Image Exploration:** "Opening and Exploring the Geo Images" tutorial

### Tools & Applications

- **Python SDK:** api.capellaspace.com access
- **SLC Data Reader:** Python module to convert Capella SLC images to amplitude images
- Capella Space official tools and documentation

### Relevant Publications

- "Analyzing LiDAR and SAR data with Capella Space and TileDB" by Stavros Papadopoulos
- "Open SAR data and scalable analytics" by Norman Barker
- "Radar Generalized Image Quality Equation Applied to Capella Open Data" by Wade Schwartzek et al.

---

## SUBMISSION & EVALUATION CRITERIA

### Submission Format

**Initial Submission (Before April 6):**
- Concise document describing contribution
- Must include:
  - Overarching idea or goal
  - Methods or techniques applied
  - Results obtained with dataset
  - Visualizations, examples, and figures
  - Optional: animations, videos, supplemental materials (via download links)
- Focus: How approach leverages large temporal stacks and value proposition
- Submit via Google Form (URL provided): https://forms.gle/gnmu1fKJAqNcxbK98
- Alternative submission: Email to dfc26@googlegroups.com with:
  - Primary Contact Name (First Name Last Name)
  - Primary Contact Affiliation (University/Organization)
  - Primary Contact Email
  - Country (Optional)
  - Team Members List (Format: Name – Affiliation – Email)
  - Link to Source Code (e.g., GitHub)
  - Confirmation of single-team participation

**Final Submission for Winners (April 20 Deadline):**
- 4-page IEEE-style paper (exclusive of references)
- IGARSS 2026 full paper template
- Describes problem, methodology, results, and insights
- Must include team member names and affiliations

### Evaluation Criteria

Committee evaluates submissions based on:

1. **Soundness and Technical Correctness**
   - Method scientifically sound and correctly implemented
   - Reasonable assumptions and valid conclusions
   - Proper methodology execution

2. **Originality and Creativity**
   - Novel ideas and approaches
   - Creative use of data
   - Unconventional problem framing or exploration
   - Innovative solutions

3. **Insightfulness**
   - Meaningful understanding of data characteristics
   - New perspectives on remote sensing problems
   - Discovery of patterns or phenomena
   - Can arise from methodological innovation or data analysis

4. **Usefulness and Practical Relevance**
   - Methods or findings improve analysis workflows
   - Enable new applications
   - Provide tools for interpretation and understanding
   - Real-world operational value

5. **Effective Use of Dataset**
   - Leverages dense temporal stacks and acquisition diversity
   - Strong use of temporal information viewed favorably
   - Spatial diversity exploitation
   - Geometric variability considerations

6. **Computational Efficiency or Scalability**
   - Addresses large-scale dataset processing (optional criterion)
   - Efficiency considerations relevant to operational use

7. **Clarity and Quality of Presentation**
   - Well-structured and understandable submission
   - Claims supported by evidence or results
   - Clear communication of methods and findings

8. **Quality of Visuals and Illustrations**
   - Figures, plots, and visualizations informative
   - Helpful for understanding approach and results
   - Professional presentation quality

9. **Reproducibility and Transparency (Required)**
   - Must make implementation publicly available (GitHub)
   - Sufficiently clear implementation
   - Described method understandable and potentially replicable
   - Adds scientific value through transparency

---

## AWARDS & PRIZES

### Recognition & Eligibility

**Winners:** First to fourth-ranked teams

**Requirements for Winning Teams:**
1. Share code openly (e.g., GitHub repository)
2. Present approaches in dedicated DFC26 session at IGARSS 2026
3. Contribute to community through open-source publication

### Awards Include:

- **IEEE Certificates of Recognition**
- **Award presentation during IGARSS 2026** (Washington, USA, August 2026)
- **Publication in IGARSS 2026 Proceedings** (4-page papers)
- **Co-authorship on Journal Paper:**
  - Summarizes DFC26 outcomes
  - Published in IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Applied Earth Observation and Remote Sensing (JSTARS)
  - Open-access publication costs supported by contest organizers
  - Includes contest organizers and all winning teams as co-authors

---

## RULES OF THE GAME

### Participation Rules

1. **Data Download:** Openly downloadable from Capella Space Open Data
2. **Contest Terms:** Participants must read and accept Contest Terms and Conditions
3. **Submission Method:** Submit PDF via Google Form (https://forms.gle/gnmu1fKJAqNcxbK98) or email to dfc26@googlegroups.com
4. **Supplemental Materials:** Animations, figures, videos can be submitted via download links in submission
5. **Submission Timeline:** Accept submissions February 4 - April 6, 2026
6. **Paper Requirements:** Maximum 4 pages (exclusive of references), using IGARSS 2026 template
7. **Team Composition:** One person can only be member of ONE team; adding team members after submission is NOT possible
8. **Organizational Conflict:** Persons directly involved in contest organization (co-organizers, organizers) cannot participate
9. **Confidentiality:** IADF TC members excluded from organization information to ensure fair competition

### Disqualification Rules

Failure to follow any of these rules will result in:
- Automatic disqualification
- Submission NOT evaluated
- Disqualification from contest

### Submission Restrictions

- Participants should NOT submit extended abstract version to IGARSS 2026
- Only top 4 ranking submissions will submit 4-page papers to IGARSS
- Winners' manuscripts reviewed by DFC Committee
- Winners submit final papers by April 28, 2026 for IGARSS inclusion

### Ranking & Evaluation

- Based on criteria described in Evaluation Section
- Committee selects winners based on overall evaluation
- Winners announced April 13, 2026
- Winners receive feedback for final manuscript preparation

---

## KEY TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS

### Data Characteristics

- **X-Band SAR** (Capella Space constellation)
- **Very High Resolution** imagery
- **Dense Temporal Sampling** enabling time-series analysis
- **Diverse Acquisition Geometry** (multiple incidence angles, look directions, orbits)
- **InSAR Compatible** SLC products enabling interferometric processing
- **Multi-Mode Coverage** (Spotlight, Sliding Spotlight, Stripmap)

### Data Scale

- **~1,582 unique collects** in coordinated stacks
- **17,000+ possible pairs** for comparative analysis
- **Global geographic distribution**
- **Multiple collection epochs** throughout the year

### Technical Focus

- Robust algorithm development
- Real-world operational diversity handling
- Deep neural network applications
- Temporal analysis methodologies
- Multi-temporal change detection
- Interferometric processing capabilities

---

## CONTACT & SUPPORT

**Primary Contact:** dfc26@googlegroups.com

**Organizers:** Image Analysis and Data Fusion Technical Committee of IEEE GRSS and Capella Space

**Questions:** Contact organizers at dfc26@googlegroups.com
